context_attestation.notes: Initial context audited before file access; no forbidden project context identified. Read only README.md, assignment.json, capsule.json and the enumerated trace; directly inspected the four permitted image attachments.

observations: All four images show a barred gate and the tutorial prompt to scan the Moon lock. None shows an opened gate or the player traversing its threshold.
Image 002 shows the player beside the right end of the token-track prop. The single perspective does not clearly establish penetration or the clearance between their surfaces.
Images 003 and 004 show the gate partly outside the left frame, with the player visible on the floor. No unambiguous view through a solid wall is visible in these stills.
The trace records leftward movement from [0,0,-28] to [-1.12,0,-28], followed by the same position under continued input.
The trace records camera yaw changing from 0 to -15.4. It supplies no intermediate camera frames, camera positions or geometry bounds.
The trace also records keyboard and touch movement and animation state changes; it contains no gate-opening, closed-gate traversal or wall-contact sequence.
interpretation: The unchanged position under continued leftward input supports blocking at one sampled prop approach. It does not independently establish that the collision boundary matches the visible prop. No definite physicality defect is established by the supplied stills, but door traversal, wall collision and clipping during camera movement remain unresolved. The trace's passed flags are not proof of those properties.
uncertainties: Whether the player's visible body penetrates the token-track prop at contact or from other approach directions.
Whether closed gates and walls block traversal and opened gates permit traversal consistently with their visible geometry.
Whether intermediate orbit or zoom positions expose clipping or impossible spatial behavior.
Only still images and a recorded trace were inspected; no live play or continuous motion inspection occurred.
counterexample_attempt: Inspected the player–prop contact in image 002 for visible interpenetration and compared images 001, 003 and 004 for exposed wall interiors, gate intersections and inconsistent spatial placement. No decisive counterexample was visible. Checked the trace for continued movement after contact: its repeated endpoint supports blocking in that instance, but missing geometry bounds and intermediate frames prevent stronger conclusions.
